overview: This bill, called the RISE Act, aims to make it easier for college students with disabilities to get accommodations such as extra test time or note-taking help. Colleges that take part in federal student aid programs would have to accept a range of existing proof of disability, including a high school special education plan (an IEP) or a Section 504 plan used at any point in high school, a record from another college, an evaluation by a licensed professional, or documentation of a military service-connected disability, rather than requiring new testing. Colleges would also have to clearly explain how they decide who qualifies for accommodations and share that information with students, parents and faculty, including on a public website. In addition, colleges would report data on how many students are registered with their disability services office, how many receive accommodations, and how many earn degrees, and the bill authorizes $10 million over fiscal years 2027 through 2031 for a national center that gives information and technical help on this topic. As of August 5, 2026, a Senate committee had approved it and it was placed on the Senate calendar.
for: Supporters say students who already had their disability documented in high school shouldn't have to pay for costly new evaluations to get help in college, and that clearer rules and data would help families choose schools.
against: Critics say requiring colleges to accept older high school records could limit their ability to judge a student's current needs, and that the new reporting requirements add paperwork for schools.
